transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-07-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Solutions), Sana Malik (NexaHealth CTO), Hank Rivera (Lead ML Eng), Priya Desai (Platform Eng), Oliver Grant (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick sync on onboarding tasks, access, and test readiness. Checklist: VPC peering, service account + keys, sample data for evals, bench schedule.

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - 1) infra access status, 2) results from the small tuning we did, 3) plan for the end-to-end bench next week, and 4) any open security items. sound good?
[00:12] Sana: yep, sounds good. just want to make sure we get the peering sorted today if possible, it's been the blocker.
[00:18] Priya: sorry i have updates - we opened the peering request but we need the exact CIDR from you and the proposed egress ports, so we can get net team to accept.
[00:26] Aisha: okay, we have the CIDR for the managed subnet - let me put that in the notes. Marco, what ports do we recommend?
[00:33] Marco: generally we just need outbound 443 and the ephemeral high ports for grpc if they run internal proxies. also if they're doing KMS calls to their cloud hsm, allow 443 to kms endpoints. i can paste the exact list after.
[00:45] Priya: perfect. also we need the service account key format - are you using ephemeral tokens or a static service account for the POC?
[00:52] Liam: for the POC we recommend short-lived service tokens via our connector, but we can support a static credential if your security team requires it. ephemeral is easier for rotation.
[01:05] Oliver: security perspective - ephemeral is preferred. we just need the audit log location and retention policy, plus whether we can push logs to our logging project. can you share the audit log doc?
[01:15] Aisha: yes, i'll send the SOC2 summary and the audit log config. we'll also include our recommended retention and an option to stream logs to your project via forwarder.
[01:26] Hank: quick question - we ran the small tuning you suggested (kv cache turned on, batch size lowered) and saw latency dip for short prompts but tail latency spiked on some sequences. not sure if we misconfigured.
[01:38] Marco: ok can you share the exact seq length distribution? tail spikes usually mean cache misses or cold kv warming. did you enable prefix caching and warm up with representative traffic?
[01:46] Hank: we warmed with a small sample but maybe not representative. i'll pull sample distribution and send. one weird thing - some tokens look garbled in the transcripts we got back, like names changing. could be model differences?
[01:58] Marco: possible. are you using our curated small-llm or a different variant? model version mismatches can cause slight output differences. we should pin a model config for the bench.
[02:09] Sana: pinning is fine. budget question - we want to avoid large reserved commit during pilot, are there cost controls to limit spend?
[02:17] Aisha: yes, we can set hard quotas on tokens and a per-route throttle; also suggest a burst cap and alerting. i'll include an example pricing sheet and quota config.
[02:29] Priya: on network - our infra team also asked about egress IP ranges for allowlists rather than peering. is that an option?
[02:36] Marco: for hosted calls yes egress IPs can be allowlisted but for the Private/VPC flow you'd want peering. allowlisting is less ideal for scale and ip churn can be a pain, but it's doable for early testing.
[02:50] Oliver: do you support KMS integration? our policy requires that the keys are customer-managed for production. for POC, we can use your managed keys but need to test the integration.
[02:58] Liam: we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and can do a test integration during the POC. we'll document options in the sheet.
[03:08] Aisha: next, bench plan - Marco, can you summarize what you'll run next week?
[03:13] Marco: sure. plan is: 1) connectivity validation, 2) end-to-end E2E run with synthetic traffic at low QPS then step to 500 and 1k QPS for a short burst, 3) measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and throughput. we'll also run a sample quality regression on the 100 prompt set Hank provides. estimate ~2 hours to run and collate.
[03:36] Hank: that's great. i'll get the 100 prompt set by friday. also we have a GDPR data question - some prompts reference pii, can you confirm logs are redacted?
[03:47] Marco: logs can be configured to redact or not capture full prompts. we'll note the default is to capture request metadata and limited context; redaction rules can be applied in the forwarder.
[03:57] Sana: timeline check - if we get peering by next week, and bench runs succeed, can we present results to procurement the following Tuesday?
[04:05] Aisha: yes, seems realistic. procurement wants cost-per-token and SLA terms - i'll prep a short deck.
[04:12] Priya: small gotcha - our net team requires a peering template with exact routes to avoid back-and-forth. can you share that?
[04:19] Aisha: yes i'll attach the peering template in the notes.
[04:24] Oliver: any compliance docs beyond SOC2/ISO - do you have pen test reports or third-party assessment?
[04:31] Liam: we have a pen test summary and a few red-team findings; will include sanitized excerpts.
[04:36] Marco: one more technical note - for the bench we need to verify KV cache warm-up. recommend a short 10-15 minute warm-up with representative prefix traffic before the 1k burst. otherwise p99s will look bad.
[04:48] Hank: ok we'll craft the warm-up script.
[04:51] Aisha: cool - any blockers left?
[04:53] Priya: just awaiting the CIDR and egress list, plus the service account spec.
[04:58] Aisha: i'll send those in email right after this call. Marco will own the bench. Hank and Priya will provide samples.
[05:05] Sana: thanks, this was helpful. let's reconvene same time next week, same place.

Recap (auto):
- Redwood to share security + network docs and pricing sheet (Aisha).
- Customer to provide VPC peering details, sample prompts, and firewall rules (Priya/Hank).
- SE to run E2E bench with KV warm-up and share metrics (Marco).
- Proposed follow-up deep-dive on latency tuning.

Links shared: Peering template (link placeholder), SOC2 summary (link placeholder), bench plan doc (link placeholder).

End of transcript.
